quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is usually the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and them.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes things more dangerous because they will follow you at a faster speed.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: If you are carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control, and hold onto passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you maintain?

options.text: At least four seconds behind the vehicle ahead.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least four seconds behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should maintain at least four seconds of following distance. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on a slippery surface. You can use the front brake on wet pavement if you apply it slowly to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is allowed if traffic is heavy.
Is allowed during the day to reduce traffic.
Is okay if you feel comfortable doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street. It is illegal.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's space cushion should:

options.text: Always stay the same.
Change based on road and weather conditions.
Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and other vehicles if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: The front brake should be:

options.text: Too dangerous for new riders to use.
Used by itself.
Used occasionally to help the rear brake.
Used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: You should choose your lane position to:

options.text: Reduce your space cushion and be seen by others.
Increase your space cushion and be seen by others.
Increase your chances of hitting road hazards and let others pass.
Reduce your chances of hitting hazards and follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your space cushion and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears. Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion.

questions.question: Before you ride, check all of the following except the:

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Up to a judge to decide.
Not too harsh.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from the elements
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting the distance ridden in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not take artificial stimulants. When they wear off, you may become dangerously tired.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever to shift up to a higher gear. Push the lever down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will go on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What should you use to make a normal stop?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for special situations.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for special situations.
Sharply squeeze the front brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. If you practice using both brakes every time, you will be ready to use them correctly in a quick stop.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: If a load is too high, it raises the center of gravity.
If a load is too high, it may interfere with the turn signals.
It may be difficult to see over a load that is placed too high.
Others can't see your load if it is low.

questions.correctAnswerText: If a load is too high, it raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load that is too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity. This affects the motorcycle's balance and stability.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: In rain, do not ride down the center of your lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars in front of you. The left tire track is usually best, but it can vary based on traffic.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Allow you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that keeps you safe. It should keep you out of other vehicles' blind spots, help you see and be seen, help you avoid hazards, avoid wind blasts, and give you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: Which gives a rider the best protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Use no lights.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid hazards, wind, and blind spots. It shows others your intentions and gives you an escape route. Lane position does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Only look five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your bike. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid dangers.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while riding?

options.text: Never
Once in a while
Often
More than you look ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Often
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. This helps you spot dangers early.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to reduce crash risk?

options.text: Wear dark clothes.
Wear bright clothes.
Do not ride during the day.
Find safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. This makes you more visible to other drivers, even during the day. Better visibility reduces crash risk.
